questions.stem: A 71-year-old man has 3 years of slowly worsening shortness of breath on exertion. For 25 years he fitted pipes and installed insulation in a naval shipyard. He has smoked a pack of cigarettes a day for 40 years. Fine crackles are heard at both lung bases. CT of the chest shows reticular fibrosis in both lower lobes and calcified plaques on the parietal pleura and the domes of the diaphragm. Pulmonary function tests show a restrictive pattern with a low DLCO. Which malignancy is this patient most likely to develop?
choices: Malignant pleural mesothelioma
Bronchogenic carcinoma
Hepatic angiosarcoma
Urothelial carcinoma of the bladder
Nasopharyngeal carcinoma
questions.explanation: Shipyard insulation work, **lower-lobe fibrosis** and **calcified pleural plaques** point to **asbestosis**. Asbestos raises the risk of both mesothelioma and lung cancer, but **bronchogenic carcinoma** is far more common in absolute terms, and asbestos and smoking **multiply** each other's effect. Mesothelioma is the most tempting choice because it is the cancer most *specific* to asbestos, yet it remains rare and smoking does not add to its risk. Hepatic angiosarcoma is linked to vinyl chloride and arsenic, not asbestos.
questions.explanation_pt: Trabalho com isolamento térmico em estaleiro, **fibrose de lobos inferiores** e **placas pleurais calcificadas** indicam **asbestose**. O asbesto (amianto) aumenta o risco de mesotelioma e de câncer de pulmão, mas o **carcinoma broncogênico** é muito mais frequente em números absolutos, e asbesto e tabagismo **multiplicam** o efeito um do outro. O mesotelioma é a opção mais tentadora por ser o câncer mais *específico* do asbesto, mas continua raro, e o tabagismo não aumenta seu risco. O angiossarcoma hepático está ligado ao cloreto de vinila e ao arsênio, e não ao asbesto.

questions.stem: A 52-year-old man who races pigeons has had repeated episodes of fever, chills, dry cough and shortness of breath over the past 6 months. Each episode starts 4 to 8 hours after he cleans his pigeon loft and fades over 1 to 2 days. He has no wheezing, no history of asthma, and his blood eosinophil count is normal. CT of the chest shows ill-defined centrilobular ground-glass nodules in both lungs. Bronchoalveolar lavage shows a marked increase in lymphocytes. Which mechanism best explains his lung disease?
choices: IgE-mediated mast cell degranulation in response to an inhaled allergen
Direct toxic injury of alveolar macrophages by inhaled mineral particles
Invasion of the lung tissue by a fungus that grows in bird droppings
Immune complex and T-cell-mediated reaction to an inhaled organic antigen
Autoantibodies directed against type IV collagen of the alveolar basement membrane
questions.explanation: Fever and cough that start **hours** after exposure to birds, with **lymphocytosis** in the lavage, fit **hypersensitivity pneumonitis** (bird fancier's lung). Inhaled bird proteins trigger a mixed **type III** (immune complex) and **type IV** (T-cell) reaction in the alveolar walls and small airways. IgE-mediated allergy is the tempting choice, but it acts within **minutes**, causes wheezing and eosinophilia, and does not cause fever. Mineral dusts cause pneumoconioses, not this organic-antigen reaction.
questions.explanation_pt: Febre e tosse que começam **horas** após a exposição a aves, com **linfocitose** no lavado, indicam **pneumonite de hipersensibilidade** (pulmão do criador de aves). As proteínas de aves inaladas desencadeiam uma reação mista **tipo III** (imunocomplexos) e **tipo IV** (linfócitos T) nas paredes alveolares e nas pequenas vias aéreas. A alergia mediada por IgE é a opção tentadora, mas age em **minutos**, causa sibilância e eosinofilia e não causa febre. As poeiras minerais causam pneumoconioses, e não esta reação a antígenos orgânicos.

questions.stem: A 47-year-old woman has 1 year of dry cough, fatigue and shortness of breath on exertion. She has never smoked and has no pets. Chest CT shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy and small nodules along the bronchovascular bundles. A transbronchial biopsy shows noncaseating granulomas, and stains for acid-fast bacilli and fungi are negative. Her blood lymphocytes proliferate strongly when they are cultured with a material that she handles every day at work. Which job history best explains her disease?
choices: Machining metal alloy parts for aircraft and electronics
Cutting, grinding and polishing granite stone for kitchen countertops
Removing old insulation from heating pipes in public buildings
Working underground in a coal mine
Harvesting and storing hay on a dairy farm
questions.explanation: Noncaseating granulomas with hilar nodes look like sarcoidosis, but a **T-cell proliferation response** to a workplace material points to **chronic beryllium disease**. Beryllium is used in **aerospace** and **electronics** alloys, and it triggers a **type IV** granulomatous reaction. Granite work causes **silicosis**, which tends to cause upper-lobe nodules and eggshell nodes, not a beryllium-specific T-cell response. Insulation work suggests asbestos, coal mining causes coal workers' pneumoconiosis, and moldy hay causes farmer's lung.
questions.explanation_pt: Granulomas não caseosos com linfonodos hilares lembram sarcoidose, mas uma **resposta proliferativa de linfócitos T** a um material do trabalho indica **doença crônica por berílio** (beriliose). O berílio é usado em ligas das indústrias **aeroespacial** e **eletrônica** e desencadeia uma reação granulomatosa **tipo IV**. O trabalho com granito causa **silicose**, que tende a produzir nódulos em lobos superiores e **calcificação em casca de ovo** dos linfonodos hilares, e não uma resposta T específica ao berílio. O isolamento térmico sugere asbesto, a mineração de carvão causa pneumoconiose dos mineiros de carvão, e o feno mofado causa pulmão do fazendeiro.

questions.stem: A 27-year-old man finished chemotherapy for a nonseminomatous testicular germ cell tumor 4 months ago. He received three drugs over 9 weeks. He now has a dry cough and shortness of breath when climbing stairs. He has never smoked. Fine crackles are heard at both lung bases. CT of the chest shows subpleural reticular opacities in both lower lobes. Pulmonary function tests show: FVC 64% of predicted, FEV1 67% of predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.86, TLC 70% of predicted, and DLCO 48% of predicted. Which drug most likely caused his lung findings?
choices: Cisplatin
Etoposide
Bleomycin
Ifosfamide
Vinblastine
questions.explanation: Low TLC with a normal FEV1/FVC and a **low DLCO** is an **intrinsic restrictive** pattern, and basal subpleural reticulation fits **drug-induced pulmonary fibrosis**. **Bleomycin**, part of the standard regimen for testicular cancer, makes **free radicals** that break DNA; the lung has little of the enzyme that inactivates it, so lung injury and fibrosis follow. Cisplatin, given with it, is the tempting choice, but its typical toxicities are **kidney damage, hearing loss and neuropathy**, not lung fibrosis.
questions.explanation_pt: CPT baixa com relação VEF1/CVF normal e **DLCO baixa** é um padrão **restritivo intrínseco**, e a reticulação subpleural basal indica **fibrose pulmonar induzida por fármaco**. A **bleomicina**, parte do esquema padrão para câncer de testículo, gera **radicais livres** que quebram o DNA; o pulmão tem pouca da enzima que a inativa, e daí resultam lesão pulmonar e fibrose. A cisplatina, dada junto, é a opção tentadora, mas suas toxicidades típicas são **lesão renal, perda auditiva e neuropatia**, e não fibrose pulmonar.

questions.stem: A 44-year-old woman is evaluated for shortness of breath on exertion before bariatric surgery. Her body mass index is 47 kg/m2. She has never smoked, and her lungs are clear to auscultation. Pulmonary function tests show: TLC 76% of predicted, FVC 74% of predicted, FEV1/FVC 0.84, expiratory reserve volume 30% of predicted, and DLCO 105% of predicted. Chest x-ray shows low lung volumes with no interstitial opacities. Which mechanism best explains her pulmonary function results?
choices: Fibrotic thickening of the alveolar interstitium
Loss of lung elastic recoil from destruction of the alveolar walls and septa
Narrowing of the small airways by bronchial smooth muscle contraction and mucus
Weakness of the diaphragm from phrenic nerve injury
Reduced chest wall compliance from excess thoracic and abdominal mass
questions.explanation: Low TLC with a normal FEV1/FVC is **restrictive**, and a **normal DLCO** shows that the gas-exchange surface is intact, so the problem is **outside the lung**. In **obesity**, fat on the chest wall and in the abdomen makes the **chest wall stiffer** and pushes the diaphragm up, so the **expiratory reserve volume** and FRC fall the most. Interstitial fibrosis is the tempting choice because it is also restrictive, but it thickens the alveolar membrane and **lowers the DLCO**. Phrenic nerve injury would also give extrinsic restriction with a normal DLCO, but nothing in her history suggests it, and her weight explains the findings.
questions.explanation_pt: CPT baixa com relação VEF1/CVF normal indica padrão **restritivo**, e uma **DLCO normal** mostra que a superfície de troca gasosa está preservada; portanto, o problema está **fora do pulmão**. Na **obesidade**, a gordura na parede torácica e no abdome **reduz a complacência da parede torácica** e eleva o diafragma, e o **volume de reserva expiratório** e a CRF são os que mais caem. A fibrose intersticial é a opção tentadora por também ser restritiva, mas ela espessa a membrana alveolar e **reduz a DLCO**. A lesão do nervo frênico também causaria restrição extrínseca com DLCO normal, mas nada na história a sugere, e o peso dela explica os achados.

questions.stem: A 63-year-old man worked for 30 years in an underground coal mine. For the past 5 years he has had symmetric pain and swelling of the small joints of both hands, and his rheumatoid factor is strongly positive. Chest x-ray shows several well-defined round nodules, 1 to 4 cm across, scattered through the periphery of both lungs, on a background of many tiny nodules in the upper zones. Biopsy of one large nodule shows a necrotic center surrounded by palisading histiocytes, with a ring of dark dust-laden macrophages. Which diagnosis best explains the large nodules?
choices: Progressive massive fibrosis
Reactivation tuberculosis
Metastatic adenocarcinoma
Caplan syndrome
Granulomatosis with polyangiitis
questions.explanation: A coal miner with **rheumatoid arthritis** who develops multiple peripheral **rheumatoid nodules** (central necrosis with **palisading histiocytes**) in a dusty lung has **Caplan syndrome**. It can also occur with silica or asbestos exposure. **Progressive massive fibrosis** is the tempting choice, but it forms large confluent fibrotic masses in the **upper lobes** from heavy dust load, without the palisading histiocytes of a rheumatoid nodule. Granulomatosis with polyangiitis can also cause necrotic nodules, but it comes with sinus and kidney disease and vasculitis, not a ring of coal dust.
questions.explanation_pt: Um mineiro de carvão com **artrite reumatoide** que desenvolve vários **nódulos reumatoides** periféricos (necrose central com **histiócitos em paliçada**) em um pulmão com poeira tem **síndrome de Caplan**. Ela também pode ocorrer com exposição a sílica ou asbesto. A **fibrose maciça progressiva** é a opção tentadora, mas forma grandes massas fibróticas confluentes nos **lobos superiores** por alta carga de poeira, sem os histiócitos em paliçada do nódulo reumatoide. A granulomatose com poliangiite também pode causar nódulos necróticos, mas vem com doença sinusal e renal e vasculite, e não com um anel de poeira de carvão.

questions.stem: A 29-year-old woman has had 2 weeks of fever, painful red nodules on the front of both shins, and swollen, tender ankles. She has a mild dry cough. Temperature is 38.1°C (100.6°F). Chest x-ray shows bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy with clear lung fields. Serum calcium and liver tests are normal. The tuberculin skin test is negative. Which course is most likely for her illness?
choices: Spontaneous remission over months without lasting lung damage
Progression to fibrotic lung disease with upper-lobe honeycombing
Transformation of the hilar nodes into lymphoma
Chronic erosive arthritis that destroys the ankle joints
Development of granulomatous myocarditis with heart block
questions.explanation: Fever, **erythema nodosum**, **ankle arthritis** and **bilateral hilar lymphadenopathy** form **Löfgren syndrome**, an acute presentation of sarcoidosis. It usually **resolves on its own** and carries the best prognosis of all forms of sarcoidosis. Progression to fibrosis is the tempting choice because it does occur in chronic sarcoidosis, but it is uncommon after Löfgren syndrome, whose ankle involvement is also non-erosive.
questions.explanation_pt: Febre, **eritema nodoso**, **artrite de tornozelos** e **linfonodomegalia hilar bilateral** formam a **síndrome de Löfgren**, uma apresentação aguda da sarcoidose. Ela geralmente **regride espontaneamente** e tem o melhor prognóstico entre as formas de sarcoidose. A progressão para fibrose é a opção tentadora porque ocorre na sarcoidose crônica, mas é incomum após a síndrome de Löfgren, cujo acometimento dos tornozelos também não é erosivo.

questions.stem: A 39-year-old man with severe acute pancreatitis develops sudden, severe shortness of breath on day 2. Chest x-ray shows new bilateral diffuse opacities, and the pulmonary capillary wedge pressure is normal. Arterial blood gas while he breathes 60% oxygen on a ventilator shows a PaO2 of 64 mm Hg. Over the next 3 weeks his oxygenation slowly improves and he is taken off the ventilator. Which cell proliferates to restore the lining of the damaged alveolar walls during his recovery?
choices: Type I pneumocytes
Type II pneumocytes
Club cells of the terminal bronchioles
Alveolar macrophages
Basal cells of the bronchial epithelium
questions.explanation: This is **ARDS** after pancreatitis: diffuse alveolar damage with loss of the **type I pneumocytes** that line most of the alveolar surface. During repair, **type II pneumocytes** divide and then differentiate into new type I cells, restoring the lining (and surfactant production). Type I pneumocytes are the tempting choice because they are the cells that must be replaced, but they are thin, terminally differentiated cells that cannot divide well. Club cells and basal cells repair the airways, not the alveoli.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **SDRA** após pancreatite: dano alveolar difuso com perda dos **pneumócitos tipo I**, que revestem a maior parte da superfície alveolar. Na reparação, os **pneumócitos tipo II** se dividem e depois se diferenciam em novas células tipo I, restaurando o revestimento (e a produção de surfactante). Os pneumócitos tipo I são a opção tentadora porque são as células que precisam ser repostas, mas são células finas, terminalmente diferenciadas, que quase não se dividem. As células club e as células basais reparam as vias aéreas, e não os alvéolos.
